title: İstanbul Limonatası
author: Yasemin Özek
description:
Dario’s life unravels after his wife, Liana, discovers that he has cheated on her for the first time in their twenty-four-year relationship. The revelation throws both of them into crisis. Dario is consumed not only by guilt over betraying the woman he loves and the family they built together, but also by confusion about his own identity. He struggles to understand whether the encounter was a fleeting exception, a long-suppressed truth, or something in between. Dario finds himself trapped between two versions of himself: the devoted husband and father he has always been, and a newly awakened side he cannot explain or control.

Running parallel to the present-day collapse of Dario’s marriage is the story of his past. Through memories stretching from his childhood in 1970s Istanbul to his teenage years on Büyükada, the novel reveals the emotional foundations of the man he became. We witness his parents’ troubled marriage, his father’s infidelity and eventual departure, and the loneliness and confusion those events left behind. These memories cast a long shadow over the present: as Dario fears becoming the very source of pain he once suffered, he confronts the possibility that his own family may now be repeating a cycle he spent a lifetime trying to escape. Spanning three decades and moving between contemporary America and the Istanbul of the 1970s and 1980s, the novel is equally a love letter to a vanished world. Through vivid memories of Büyükada - the largest of Istanbul’s Princes’ Islands - readers are immersed in long summer evenings by the sea, bicycle rides beneath pine trees, ferry journeys across the Bosphorus, family gatherings, music-filled social clubs, and the multicultural fabric of a city where Turkish, Jewish, Levantine, and Mediterranean traditions intertwined.
